reasoning.text: The render reads clearly as an FPGA NTT accelerator card: eight blue interleaved BRAM banks along the -Z edge, the open butterfly array (copper multiplier column, dark/steel symmetric add-sub pairs, white registers) framed by rails, the brass twiddle broadcast rail overhead, the reduction spine on +X, and the exploded radix-4 unit and heatsink lifted above (the SIDE view confirms both float on their risers, not in empty space). Two real geometric defects are visible/derivable: the right longitudinal rail (x=1.95, spanning 1.87..2.03) interpenetrates the full-depth Barrett q-multiplier cylinder (x=2.2, r=0.5, spanning 1.7..2.7), and that same spine crowded the pipeline-register column. The dominant remaining weakness is not visual at all — it is source fidelity: the carried reflection flags that the conflict-free bank map b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8 collides at radix-2 stages s>=6, so the spec realizes a generic NTT rather than CFNTT's headline no-conflict access, and the exact paper schedule/twiddle ordering/cycle counts remain reproduction-invented. I deliberately did NOT fabricate a replacement bank function or schedule this pass — inventing unverified arithmetic would poison the spec substrate; those belong to the reproduce loop with the paper in hand.
gaps: Source fidelity (reproduce loop, needs the paper): transcribe CFNTT's actual conflict-free bank-index b(i) and offset o(i) — the current (i+(i>>3)) mod 8 map is injective but collides for radix-2 stages s>=6, so the no-conflict claim in crossbar_network.spec.notes is an approximation, not the paper's Sec. III result. Do not invent a replacement here; pin it from the source.

Source fidelity: the radix-4 fusion is modeled as a 2x radix-2 composition; the paper's specific fused per-stage schedule and twiddle reuse that yield the quoted 33%/20% op savings are improvised in config_radix_selector.spec and schedule_controller.spec.fsm.

Source fidelity: forward/inverse decimation direction (DIT vs DIF, stride sign) and authoritative pipeline cycle counts are reproduction defaults (9 cycles/lane); reconcile against the paper before claiming buildability is complete.

Plan-view overlap: the exploded radix-4 unit (z 1.9..2.9) clears central lanes 3-4 but sits over lanes 5-6 in TOP view; if vertical headroom allows above the array but below the heatsink, raise it for cleaner plan separation.

Minor: crossbar_network.spec states '8 read + 8 write per cycle' but eight radix-2 butterflies need 16 operand reads (dual-port BRAM); make the port accounting explicit so a rebuilder is not under-provisioned.
